title: One full MCP tool-call round trip

events.label: Startup: client wired
events.detail: At startup, the host application opens one MCP client connection per server it intends to use — the client is the in-host protocol translation layer.

events.label: Handshake: initialize
events.detail: Protocol version and capability negotiation: serverA (filesystem) reports its lists of tools / resources / prompts — discovery is one-time, invocation on demand.

events.label: Handshake: initialize
events.detail: serverB (database) reports its tool list: query_orders and friends.

events.label: Capability lists returned
events.detail: What MCP deflates is integration explosion: without it, M applications × N tools demand M×N glue codebases; with it, tool builders implement one server, application builders one client — M+N.

events.label: The question
events.detail: "What was last quarter's order total? Save the details to a file." — a task spanning two servers.

events.label: Task enters the host
events.detail: The host translates human intent into model calls.

events.label: Request (merged tool list)
events.detail: Both servers' tools are merged into one list for the model — the model never senses MCP; it sees an ordinary tool list (T01).

events.label: tool_use: query_orders
events.detail: A structured request, structurally identical to T01.

events.label: Forwarded via the client
events.detail: The only difference from an ordinary tool call is where execution happens: from an in-process function to a protocol-mediated server call — routing follows server ownership.

events.label: serverB executes the query
events.detail: The database server runs the query and returns: East China Q2 order total ¥4,182,000.

events.label: serverA writes the file
events.detail: The second action travels the same client channel to the filesystem server, and the detail file lands on disk.

events.label: Results returned to the host
events.detail: Both results are paired back by tool_use id — the protocol changed a layer; the pairing rules did not.

events.label: Replied and answered
events.detail: The model writes the final answer. A security note: servers are third-party code — grant capabilities item by item and minimally; never serve up an entire filesystem at once.
